title: Client-Centred Learning
whatItIs: The approach at the heart of the National standard for driver and rider training: a conversation between learner and instructor based on mutual respect.
keyFacts: Client-centred is not client-led: the learner doesn't take charge and decide what happens.
People resist new ideas if the trainer doesn't respect them, isn't 'genuine' or lacks legitimate authority.
Just telling learners what to do may get them through the test, but they quickly forget it.
The goal is a safe, responsible method the learner applies consistently, not one set method.
Transfer responsibility for learning to the learner as soon as they're ready to take it.

a.label: Client-centred
points: A conversation based on mutual respect
Instructor still brings expertise and puts safety first

b.label: Client-led
points: The learner takes charge and decides what happens
Not what the standard asks for

onTheTest.question: What does the National standard for driver and rider training mean by 'client-centred learning'?
options: A conversation between learner and instructor based on mutual respect
The learner decides what happens on each lesson
The instructor follows a fixed syllabus for every pupil
The learner is coached and never told anything
onTheTest.why: Unit 3: client-centred learning is not about the learner taking charge of the learning process. It is a conversation between learner and instructor based on mutual respect.

onTheTest.question: A pupil clearly needs help in a situation they can't handle, but the instructor gives none. What does DVSA guidance call this?
onTheTest.why: Examiner guidance 3.24: if the pupil needs support and gets it, that's client-centred. If they need help and don't get it, that's not client-centred and is often called 'under instruction'.

traps: Coaching doesn't replace instruction: direct instruction still suits new situations or a struggling pupil.
Elements 6.3.1 to 6.3.3 are layers of one approach: they can't really be shown in isolation.
'Client-centred', 'student-centred' and 'learner-centred' mean broadly the same in the standard.
